definition: Byproduct means something produced incidentally while something else is being made.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word byproduct. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know byproduct should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Candied peel began as a byproduct: rind left over from pressing oranges for juice, too fragrant for anyone to throw away.
The product is the whole point of the process — the thing everyone came to make — while a byproduct falls out uninvited along the way; the product sits at the intended end of this scale.
Waste lies further from the point than a byproduct — a byproduct at least finds a buyer or a use; waste is the output nobody wants at any price.

A side effect is an unplanned result of an action — drowsiness from a pill, noise from roadwork — an event or condition rather than a thing. A byproduct is the unplanned thing itself that a process makes: whey, stone dust, waste heat.

A spin-off is a sideline that has grown into its own venture — a company, a series, a product line with its own name. A byproduct is earlier in that story: the incidental output as it first falls out of a process, before anyone has built anything on it.

Product rests on Latin duc-, "to lead"; an aqueduct joins it to aqua and literally leads water across a valley.
Byproduct means something produced incidentally while something else is being made.
The data center on the ring road exists to run computations, and heat is the byproduct computation always throws off.
For years, fans pushed that warmth into the sky.
The server halls now heat the public swimming pool through the winter, and the manager likes to say the town swims in arithmetic.
Byproduct is the exact word for that warmth, because it names something produced incidentally while something else is being made.
Nobody built the halls to warm a pool — the heat simply falls out of the real work — and finding a use for it is what turns an incidental output from a nuisance into an asset.
Byproduct is the accountant's honest word for the thing you made without meaning to — whey, stone dust, waste heat.
Use side effect when the incidental result is an event or condition rather than a thing, and spin-off when the sideline has grown a life of its own.
The word carries no judgment: a byproduct can be worth nothing or worth more than the product itself.

The brewery on Fifth Street measures its success in barrels, but its most loyal customers arrive for something else entirely.
Every batch of beer begins by soaking hundreds of pounds of barley, and once the sugars are drawn off, the soggy grain has done its job.
For a century such spent grain was a byproduct in the plainest sense — hauled away at the brewery's own expense, mostly to feed hogs.
Then the bakery next door asked for a share.
Spent grain, it turns out, bakes into a dense, sweet loaf, and the Tuesday bread line now rivals the taproom's.
The brewers still insist the beer is the point.
The bakers, buttering the evidence, are no longer sure.
